| Your priority | Firms to contact first |

| Chermside and nearby suburbs | Kelly Lawyers; Crouch & Co; Vicca Law |
| North Lakes and Moreton Bay | Cooke & Hutchinson; Coastside Law |
| A complex will challenge or court dispute | Attwood Marshall; Armstrong Legal |
| A claim for further provision under an FPA | Baker Hastings; Aitken Whyte; Kelly Lawyers |
| A practice focused strongly on contested estates | Estate Battles; Attwood Marshall |


These are research-based matches to the services advertised by the firms, not a guarantee of outcome or an independent assessment of their litigation success.

## 4\. Important Queensland FPA deadline

If you are considering contesting a will, **do not wait until you have selected a lawyer to check the deadline**\.

Under section 41 of Queensland’s *Succession Act 1981*, an eligible person generally must commence a Family Provision Application within **nine months of the deceased’s date of death**\. The executor or administrator should generally receive notice of the intended claim within **six months of death**\. Exceptions and court discretion can apply, so obtain advice on your particular circumstances promptly. [www.awbrisbanelawyers.com.au](https://www.awbrisbanelawyers.com.au/will-dispute-lawyers/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[kellylawyers.com.au](https://kellylawyers.com.au/services/wills-estates/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

An FPA is not the same as challenging the validity of a will. Depending on your circumstances, you may need advice about\:

- **Family Provision Application\:** you believe the deceased did not make adequate provision for you.
- **Invalid will\:** you suspect lack of testamentary capacity, undue influence, fraud, or improper execution.
- **Executor or beneficiary dispute\:** you disagree with how the estate is being administered or distributed.
- **Defending a claim\:** you are an executor or beneficiary responding to a challenge.

## 5\. Questions to ask before engaging a firm

When contacting two or three firms, ask\:

1. How much of your practice involves contested wills and Family Provision Applications, rather than estate planning?
2. Who will personally handle the matter, and what experience do they have in Queensland estate litigation?
3. What is the estimated total cost through negotiation, mediation and, if necessary, a court hearing?
4. Is a fixed-fee initial consultation available, and are there any conditional fee arrangements?
5. Given the size of the estate and your relationship to the deceased, what are the realistic prospects and potential costs risks?

**One final question that would help me narrow this down\:** Are you looking to *make* an FPA because you believe you were unfairly left out of a will, *challenge the validity* of a will, or *defend* a claim against an estate? The best-fit firms can differ depending on which side of the dispute you are on.

## 4\. Important Queensland FPA deadline

If you are considering contesting a will, **do not wait until you have selected a lawyer to check the deadline**\.

Under section 41 of Queensland’s *Succession Act 1981*, an eligible person generally must commence a Family Provision Application within **nine months of the deceased’s date of death**\. The executor or administrator should generally receive notice of the intended claim within **six months of death**\. Exceptions and court discretion can apply, so obtain advice on your particular circumstances promptly. [www.awbrisbanelawyers.com.au](https://www.awbrisbanelawyers.com.au/will-dispute-lawyers/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[kellylawyers.com.au](https://kellylawyers.com.au/services/wills-estates/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

An FPA is not the same as challenging the validity of a will. Depending on your circumstances, you may need advice about\:

- **Family Provision Application\:** you believe the deceased did not make adequate provision for you.
- **Invalid will\:** you suspect lack of testamentary capacity, undue influence, fraud, or improper execution.
- **Executor or beneficiary dispute\:** you disagree with how the estate is being administered or distributed.
- **Defending a claim\:** you are an executor or beneficiary responding to a challenge.

## 5\. Questions to ask before engaging a firm

When contacting two or three firms, ask\:

1. How much of your practice involves contested wills and Family Provision Applications, rather than estate planning?
2. Who will personally handle the matter, and what experience do they have in Queensland estate litigation?
3. What is the estimated total cost through negotiation, mediation and, if necessary, a court hearing?
4. Is a fixed-fee initial consultation available, and are there any conditional fee arrangements?
5. Given the size of the estate and your relationship to the deceased, what are the realistic prospects and potential costs risks?

**One final question that would help me narrow this down\:** Are you looking to *make* an FPA because you believe you were unfairly left out of a will, *challenge the validity* of a will, or *defend* a claim against an estate? The best-fit firms can differ depending on which side of the dispute you are on.
